title: Tokyo, Japan
overview: Tokyo is Japan's capital and one of the world's most dynamic megacities. It blends ultramodern skyscrapers, cutting-edge technology, and ancient temples in a city of extraordinary contrasts. Renowned for its world-class cuisine, impeccable public transport, and unparalleled safety, Tokyo is a dream destination for food lovers, tech enthusiasts, and culture seekers alike.
best_time_to_visit: March–May for cherry blossoms and mild weather. October–November for autumn foliage and clear skies. Avoid June–July (rainy season) and August (hot and humid).
climate: Humid subtropical. Hot summers (30–35°C) with high humidity, mild springs and autumns (15–22°C), cool winters (5–10°C). June–July is rainy season.

attractions.name: Senso-ji Temple
attractions.description: Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple in Asakusa. The Nakamise shopping street leads to the main hall. Beautiful at dawn before crowds arrive.

attractions.name: Shibuya Crossing
attractions.description: World's busiest pedestrian crossing, with over 3,000 people crossing at once. Best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park above the intersection.

attractions.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
attractions.description: 55-hectare park blending French, English, and Japanese garden styles. Best during cherry blossom season (late March–early April).

attractions.name: teamLab Borderless
attractions.description: Immersive digital art museum. Book online well in advance – sells out weeks ahead. Located in Odaiba.

attractions.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
attractions.description: The outer market remains open to visitors with dozens of stalls selling sushi, tamagoyaki, and fresh seafood. Best for a morning food walk.

attractions.name: Akihabara Electric Town
attractions.description: World centre for electronics, anime, manga, and gaming. Great for tech shopping and exploring multi-floor arcades and maid cafes.

attractions.name: Harajuku & Takeshita Street
attractions.description: Youth fashion epicentre with colourful crepe shops, eccentric streetwear, and the serene Meiji Jingu shrine nearby.

attractions.name: Mount Fuji Day Trip
attractions.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site, 100km from Tokyo. Hakone or Kawaguchiko are best bases. Climbing season July–early September.

food.name: Ramen
food.description: Tokyo-style shoyu (soy) ramen is a must. Ichiran for solo dining or Fuunji for tsukemen dipping ramen are local favourites.

food.name: Sushi Omakase
food.description: Chef's choice multi-course sushi. Sukiyabashi Jiro (Ginza) is legendary but requires booking months ahead. Many excellent options in the $50–100 range.

food.name: Izakaya Dinner
food.description: Japanese pub-style dining. Order small plates of yakitori, edamame, and sake. Shinjuku's Golden Gai has legendary tiny bars.

food.name: Convenience Store Food
food.description: 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, and Lawson in Japan serve surprisingly high-quality onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods. A budget traveller's best friend.

food.name: Tempura at Tsunahachi
food.description: Historic tempura restaurant in Shinjuku since 1923. Set menus with crispy seasonal vegetables and seafood tempura.

transport: Tokyo's rail network is world-class. Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card for seamless travel on metro, JR trains, and buses. A 7-day JR Pass is worthwhile for day trips. Taxis are expensive. The metro runs until ~midnight.

budget_guide.notes: Japan is more affordable than many visitors expect. A 7-day JR Pass costs ~$300 but covers all Shinkansen and local JR trains.

tips: Carry cash – many small shops and restaurants don't accept cards.
Bow slightly when greeting locals as a sign of respect.
No tipping – it can be considered rude in Japan.
Get a pocket WiFi or SIM card at the airport for navigation.
Last trains run around midnight; missing them means a taxi or overnight café.
